I fixed the bug: `![x\"x](x)` with smarty now gives `

`, the same as the unescaped version. Nothing is committed. **Why it happened:** a backslash escape like `\"` is stored as a placeholder while the document is being processed. The step that turned placeholders back into characters ran *after* the HTML was written out, so a raw `"` landed inside `alt="…"` without being escaped. You only saw it with smarty because smarty is what makes `"` an escapable character. **The fix:** - **`markdown/treeprocessors.py`**: a new `UnescapeTreeprocessor` (registered as `unescape`, priority 0) restores escaped characters in text and attribute values *before* the HTML is written out. Normal HTML escaping then applies, giving `"` in attributes. It runs after smarty, so escaped quotes still aren't turned into curly quotes. - **`markdown/postprocessors.py`**: the old `UnescapePostprocessor` is no longer registered by default. I kept the class so third-party code that uses or subclasses it still works, but it now raises a `DeprecationWarning` when created. **One visible output change:** `\>` now renders as `>` instead of a bare `>`. Browsers display it the same, but if anyone compares output byte-for-byte, it will differ. I updated `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html` to match. **Tests added:** - `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` (new file): escaped quotes in body text, image alt text, link titles and reference-style images. Three of these fail without the fix. - `tests/test_syntax/inline/test_images.py`: `![x\>x](x)` → `alt="x>x"`, without smarty. - `tests/test_apis.py`: checks the deprecation warning and that `unescape` is now a treeprocessor, not a postprocessor. **Docs:** I added a note and a bug-fix entry to `docs/change_log/release-3.4.md`, and updated the processor tables in `docs/extensions/api.md`. **Test results:** 948 passed and 12 failed. The same 12 fail without my change: they're raw-HTML/`md_in_html` tests (unclosed tags, comments). The collection error in `test_md_in_html.py::TestSuite` was also already there. I couldn't run flake8 because it isn't installed in the venv.
